A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JoVA and retain identifiable architecture, losses, experiments, and appendix validation material. Their complete text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite v2's substantial extension to editing.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation comparisons, mouth-loss and attention ablations, model-scaling experiments, and appendix mouth-mask validation.

after.justification: v2 reports original generation and editing experiments, architecture ablations, JoVA's VBench results, and a human evaluation with 21 participants.

M1.justification: v2 extends generation to joint editing through reference-audio token concatenation and reference-video/image conditioning with a binary mask, channel concatenation, and a projector (Section 3.2). These change the supported inputs and procedure beyond v1's text/image-conditioned generation. Joint attention, flow matching, and the mouth-area loss remain.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's natural-scene and human-speech generation coverage, v2 trains on video editing, audio editing, joint editing, and reconstruction tasks. It adds JoVABench-Edit evaluations covering background, style, and local modifications, plus VBench video-generation evaluation. The corresponding generation comparison appearing as JoVABench-Gen is not counted as new coverage merely because its name changes.

E2.justification: JavisDiT enters both generation comparisons; LTX-2 and UniAVGen enter JoVABench-Gen. The editing comparison adds Ditto, ICVE, InsViE, Lucy, and OmniVideo, each combined with Diff2Lip or Wav2Lip. Appendix A additionally compares against video generators using borrowed baseline scores. These are substantial additions to actual comparisons, including methods only cited in v1.

E3.justification: Reported joint training changes from 50K steps at 5e-5 to 100K steps at 3e-5 and includes editing. New evaluations introduce LSE-D, FC, IB-TV, and DeSync; IS is now specified on video frames rather than described as an audio metric. Appendix B adds blind 1–5 MOS evaluation with 21 participants and 50 samples per task.

E4.justification: v1's temporal-RoPE ablation and smaller-backbone scaling study are removed. v2 adds an Ovi-style sequential cross-attention variant to the fusion ablation and editing case studies examining instruction following and unintended changes. The mouth-loss ablation remains, and the existing mouth-mask validation moves from Appendix A to Appendix E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, dispersion estimates, or significance tests. The new human-evaluation tables report mean scores only; their participant and sample counts describe the new evaluation protocol rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: JoVA's reported Verse-Bench results change, including LSE-C 6.51 to 6.65, FD 1.10 to 0.82, and MS 0.80 to 0.75. These accompany changed training and are not controlled same-setting gains. v2 adds editing results, including LSE-C 5.88 and LSE-D 1.66, VBench total score 82.61, and human ratings. Generation and ablation entries are also revised, while RoPE and smaller-model results disappear.

T1.justification: v2 omits v1's explicit floor/ceiling spatial-coordinate mapping and min/max temporal bounding-box definition (Section 3.2.2, Equation 5), retaining only a higher-level description. The transformer, flow-matching, joint-attention, and mouth-loss mathematics otherwise remain equivalent; neither version provides theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions, and conclusion expand the central claim from synchronized video-audio generation to a single framework for generation and editing. The approximately 3M-pair corpus, editing-data synthesis pipeline, and generation/editing benchmarks become central contributions, replacing the earlier emphasis on mouth supervision as a separate headline contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving preservation of pretrained priors and avoidance of cascading editing errors, and qualifies editing comparisons by noting baselines receive ground-truth audio. It newly identifies fast-hand artifacts, failures to preserve background text, and human-speech-only editing coverage caused by limited paired data. v1's RoPE trade-off and small-model deployment interpretations are removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents an editing-data pipeline using GPT-4o, FLUX.1-Kontext-dev, Wan2.2 control, Qwen3, and Higgs-Audio, alongside conditioning-mask conventions and detailed editing-task distributions. These substantially expand implementation information. Conversely, explicit mouth-box mapping formulas and v1's total-parameter accounting are omitted. The project-page access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around joint generation and joint editing. v2 adds positioning against unified video editors and audiovisual editing systems, including VACE, UniVideo, OpenVE-3M, Object-AVEdit, and lip-sync methods, as well as newer generation work such as LTX-2. The claimed distinction now concerns unified generation/editing rather than primarily simpler synchronized generation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and related-work discussion are extensively rewritten. The method is reorganized around architecture, conditioning, and objectives; dataset composition receives a separate section; and the appendix expands into sections A–F. The former 'Quantitative Results' heading for qualitative examples is also corrected.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening architectural comparison with a capabilities montage, redraws the main architecture and data pipelines, and adds dataset charts, editing comparisons, training examples, and new tables. The fusion table changes structure, while existing generation and mouth-mask illustrations are relocated. The new Figure 2 reverses the generation/editing labels on its example prompts.

improvement.justification: v2 turns v1's largely prospective task-extensibility claim into an implemented editing capability supported by comparative experiments. Broader generation baselines, the added Ovi-style attention control, and blind human evaluation substantially strengthen the evidence beyond v1's automatic metrics and selected examples. Specific failure conditions also clarify applicability. These gains outweigh the removed RoPE/scaling analyses and reduced mouth-mask implementation detail, although uncertainty estimates remain absent and some presentation errors persist.
